finding: TEST-5 carried [acceptance][invariant: INV-3] and claimed to prove the store's hasPermissionNow self-gate is load-bearing. It does not: the server-update MODULE declares `shouldLoad: ctx => ctx.isAuthenticated && ctx.can(Permissions.ServerUpdateRead)` (modules/server-update/module.tsx:26), so for an unpermitted user the module never loads and the store init() never runs. Deleting the store gate leaves TEST-5 green — a D2 tautology: the test cannot fail when the invariant it pins is violated. FIXED: added TEST-7/TEST-8 over the memory tier (module gated only on isAuthenticated, so the store genuinely initializes) and moved the acceptance tag to TEST-8. Falsifiability VERIFIED BY RUNNING: replacing the gate with `if (true)` makes TEST-8 fail ('issued 1 request(s)'); restored, it passes.

TEST-6's first draft asserted the filtered-out conversation was gone using an UNSCOPED page.getByText(beta). The sidebar's recent-conversations widget renders the same titles from a separate, deliberately unfiltered `recentConversations` cursor, so the locator resolved to 1 element and the test went red. Worse than the red: unscoped, the assertion could never distinguish 'search filtered the list' from 'search did nothing'. FIXED: scoped every assertion to the `chat-conversation-list-rows` container; re-run PASS.

The originally-planned instrument (Playwright page.on('request'|'response') around page.goto, copied from boot-parallelism.spec.ts) over-counts across a navigation: it also catches requests the PREVIOUS document had in flight. It reported 3 both before AND after the ConversationList fix, which would have supported the false conclusion that the fix changed nothing. FIXED: replaced with a passthrough window.fetch observer installed via addInitScript, recording location.pathname so calls are attributable to the /chats document. boot-tier-permission-gate.spec.ts keeps the original helper deliberately — it compares two endpoints WITHIN one boot, where the contamination is irrelevant.

Considered: the new early-return means the effect returns no cleanup on the skipped pass, potentially leaking a timer set by a previous pass. Rejected — React runs the PREVIOUS effect's cleanup before the next run, so any outstanding timer is cleared by its own cleanup; the skipped pass has no timer to clean. Traced the type-then-erase ordering explicitly: local 'x' (timer set) -> user clears -> prev cleanup clears the timer -> new run sees local '' === store '' -> skip. Net effect: nothing fires, which is correct (the user typed and erased; the store was never filtered).

Considered: React.StrictMode (enabled at main.tsx:8) double-invokes effects in dev, so the guard could double-fire or double-skip. Rejected — the guard is idempotent: on mount both passes see local === store === '' and skip; when a timer is set, React's cleanup between passes clears it. StrictMode is in fact an additional argument FOR the change: the removed ConversationList mount fetch was double-invoked in dev.

Considered: removing ConversationList's mount fetch could strand a mount path where the parent did not just fetch. Enumerated every path — (a) page mount -> page effect fetches -> loading flips -> list mounts (covered); (b) bulk-delete drains to empty -> list UNMOUNTS to the empty state, and a later sync refetch repopulates the store before it remounts (covered); (c) error -> list mounts on the error arm and its ErrorState offers retry, which calls the store action directly (covered); (d) search empties the result -> hasSearch keeps the list mounted (covered); (e) route re-entry -> page remounts -> page effect fires (covered). Rejected as a defect; TEST-2/TEST-3 exercise (a) and the create-after-prime case on the real path rather than arguing it.

Considered: `ChatHistory.$.searchQuery` could throw or read stale if the lazy store handle is not yet resolved when the effect runs. Rejected — `$` is a first-class accessor on the store-kit handle (sdk/packages/framework/src/store-kit.ts:590 `if (prop === '$') return api.getState()`), and the component already destructures reactive fields from ChatHistory during render (ConversationList.tsx:57-68), so the store is resolved before any effect runs. `.$` is also the CORRECT choice here: a reactive proxy read is a hook and would be illegal outside render.

Considered: createTestUser might leave the restricted user holding the permission under test, making both negative tests vacuous. Verified in the backend — POST /api/users (modules/user/handlers/user.rs:180-203) auto-assigns the new user to the DEFAULT group (Users). Grepped src-app/server/migrations-merged/ for grants: `server_update::` returns zero rows and `memory::admin` returns zero rows, so neither permission is in the Users group; both restricted users genuinely lack the permission under test. (Note this DID rule out an alternative isolation target: notifications::read IS granted to Users by 202607146080, so a notification-based test would have been vacuous.)

Considered: the window.fetch instrumentation could alter app behaviour, swallow errors, or leak into production. Rejected — it lives only under src-app/ui/tests/, is installed per-test via page.addInitScript, wraps the record in try/catch so instrumentation can never break the app, and returns origFetch.apply(this, args) so every request still reaches the real server unchanged. It is an observer, not a mock: no page.route, no stubbed response, no altered status.

No API surface changed: no Rust handler/model/permission/SyncEntity touched, so openapi.json and api-client/types.ts are byte-unchanged in BOTH ui and desktop/ui and no `just openapi-regen` is implied. Verified the diff touches only two .tsx files plus two new spec files plus lifecycle artifacts.

No accessibility impact: the product diff contains ZERO JSX/markup/className/data-testid changes (verified by grepping the diff for element, className and data-testid tokens — the only matches are the words `<ConversationList>` inside prose comments). Rendered output is byte-identical; the change is an effect removal plus an effect guard.
No user-visible string added, removed or altered anywhere in the diff. All added text is code comments and test assertion messages.

Net performance effect is positive and measured: a cold /chats load drops from 3 to 1 GET /api/conversations. The added cost is one string comparison per run of an effect that already existed. No new render, no new subscription (the guard uses the NON-subscribing snapshot, so it does not widen the component's reactive surface).

Conforms to agent-kit/docs/CODING_GUIDELINES.md section 12 (frontend store discipline): the route page owns the load, the child list consumes store state. Also conforms to the reactive-read rule (`.$` outside render, never the reactive proxy). Test placement mirrors the predecessor net-hygiene lifecycle's tests/e2e/perf/ location and its real-backend/no-page.route convention.

The change narrows a boundary rather than widening one: ConversationList loses a data-fetching responsibility and becomes a presentational consumer of store state, leaving one owner for the route-level fetch. No new cross-module coupling; no new import added to either product file.

Considered: making the page the sole fetcher makes ConversationList unusable by a future second consumer that is not ChatHistoryPage. Real but acceptable and deliberate — a future consumer would own its own fetch, exactly as the single-owner contract states, and both files now carry that contract as an explicit comment ('Do not add a second caller') so the next author is told rather than left to rediscover the duplicate. Recorded as a tradeoff, not a defect.

Both changed sites carry a comment explaining WHY (the reloadQueued replay; the equal-to-store rather than first-run guard shape), cite the measurement artifact, and name the guarding spec. The guard's shape rationale is the non-obvious part and is documented at the point of the code, which is what stops a future 'simplification' to a first-run ref from silently stranding a user in a filtered list.

Verified the surviving page-level fetch is genuinely ON the runtime path rather than merely present: TEST-2 (seeded list renders, no empty state) and TEST-3 (a conversation created AFTER the store was primed still appears) both drive the real backend through the UI and pass. The measurement additionally shows exactly one request still occurring, so the fetch is not just reachable but observed.

Reconciled every PLAN ITEM against shipped code. ITEM-1 measurement -> MEASUREMENTS.md with before/after and attribution. ITEM-2 -> ConversationList.tsx effect removed, ChatHistoryPage.tsx contract documented. ITEM-3 -> TEST-2/TEST-3 green. ITEM-4 -> verdict recorded, TEST-4/5/7/8 green. ITEM-5 -> [DESCOPED] with an approved disposition in DECISIONS.md DEC-2. ITEM-6 -> debounce guard shipped, TEST-1/TEST-6 green. No item is covered on paper but absent in code.

Checked the shipped BEHAVIOUR against each invariant, not against PLAN.md. INV-1 (do not regress correctness for fewer requests): TEST-2/TEST-3/TEST-6 pass on the real path, and the search filter-then-clear leg — the one the guard could plausibly have broken — is explicitly exercised. INV-2 (one shared store read, not N callers): measured 3 -> 1, and TEST-1's assertion is falsifiable (the same instrument reported 3 on the unmodified tip). INV-3 (store self-gates the refetch): unchanged in product code, and now pinned by TEST-8, whose falsifiability was verified by breaking the gate and observing red. No behaviour satisfies the plan while violating an invariant.

[blind round] TEST-3 was VACUOUS: `page.getByText(later).first()` was unscoped, and the sidebar RecentConversationsWidget renders conversation titles on every authenticated route from the separate `recentConversations` cursor — `later` being newest, it always sat at the top of that list. The assertion passed whether or not /chats' own list refetched. FIXED: scoped to `chat-conversation-list-rows`.

[blind round] TEST-3's premise was destroyed before its assertion ran: both hops used page.goto(), a full document navigation that reloads the SPA and wipes every in-memory store, so it was an ordinary cold load (a duplicate of TEST-2), never the primed-store remount it claimed. FIXED: the round trip is now client-side (header new-chat button = router pushState, then page.goBack() = popstate) and a window marker set before the trip is asserted after it, so a reintroduced reload fails the test instead of silently degrading it.

[blind round] TEST-2's assertion was unscoped (same sidebar problem) and its backstop did not close the gap: a permanently-loading list renders the spinner branch while the page suppresses its empty state, so `expect('No chat history yet').toHaveCount(0)` passed on a stuck list. FIXED: scoped to the rows container, which renders only on the non-spinner branch. A separate 'not spinning' assertion was drafted and REMOVED after checking the source — the spinner branch carries no testid, so it would have been vacuously true.

[blind round] recordApi keyed on the RESPONSE event, so a request that was aborted, still in flight at the cutoff, or failed at the network layer was invisible — fatal for assertions of the form 'issued ZERO requests'. FIXED: records on the `request` event; the response event only fills in end/status.

[blind round] TEST-4's causality assertion compared Date.now() stamps taken in the NODE process at CDP event delivery, which is asynchronous and reorders under load — spurious failures on a busy box, or a masked real overlap. FIXED: ordering is now judged on the browser's own clock via performance.getEntriesByType('resource').

[blind round] TEST-7/TEST-8 were a CROSS-PERSONA pair: the positive control ran as admin, the negative as a restricted user, so 'the store initialized' was inferred across identities — if MemoryStatusPill stopped mounting for non-admins, TEST-8 would go vacuously green. FIXED: TEST-8 asserts a same-persona witness (the restricted user's own memory-status-pill must be visible, proving the component mounted and read MemoryAdmin.settings), and both tests now run on the same /chat/{id} surface. Measured first that no weaker witness exists: a restricted user's boot issues NO /api/memory/* request at all, so the network alone cannot distinguish 'gate fired' from 'store never initialized'.

[blind round] A load-bearing comment stated the ordering backwards: 'when it does mount it is strictly after this fetch has already started'. React runs CHILD effects BEFORE parent effects, so on an SPA re-entry with a primed store the list's effects run first. Harmless functionally, but it is the documentation justifying 'do not add a second caller'. FIXED: the justification now rests on COVERAGE (the list does not mount in the empty state), and the real ordering is stated.

[blind round] The guard comment treated setSearchQuery as a pure setter; it unconditionally issues loadConversations(1), so an equal→equal pass suppresses a REFETCH, not a redundant assignment. Concrete consequence: an 'a'→'ab'→'a' round trip after a FAILED load no longer self-heals (the user takes the ErrorState's explicit Retry). FIXED: stated precisely in the comment rather than implied away.

[blind round] Under a DEV build React.StrictMode double-invokes the surviving page effect, so the second call replays via reloadQueued and the cold load is not 'exactly one' there. ACCEPTED, not code-changed: StrictMode double-invocation is deliberate and apps must tolerate it, and the underlying wart (reloadQueued replaying an identical page-1 request) is pre-existing store behaviour outside this round's scope. The OVERCLAIM was fixed — the spec header now scopes the measurement to the PRODUCTION build the harness serves (vite preview), which is what ships.

[blind round] The 'exactly ONE' claim is narrower than stated: re-entering /chats while the store holds a stale non-empty searchQuery still yields two requests (the list mounts filtered, then its debounce commits the empty input). ACCEPTED, not code-changed — pre-existing and orthogonal to both callers removed here; documented as an explicit scope limit in the spec header.

[blind round] TEST-4/TEST-7 are both admin boots and TEST-5/TEST-8 both restricted-user boots, so four full harness boots (each its own Postgres DB + server + vite preview) carry the information of two. NOT TAKEN: merging would collapse four distinct TEST-IDs onto two test bodies, trading a clear 1:1 ID↔assertion mapping for ~40s of suite time.
